summary: Reconciliation of two validated math_and_collision proposals into one conservative engine map. Subsystem-level: four functional groups (collision-geometry/spatial-query, math-and-vector primitives, packed vector codecs, sparse constraint solvers) covering all 18 required functions. Type families: eight canonical families carried 1:1 from the eight class proposals; none are merged because cross-proposal common ownership is not proven (only shared data layout). Notable overlap observed: CollisionModel (0x00403640) and SpatialNearestNeighborQuery (0x004038E0) both run nearest-neighbor queries over the same 316-byte-stride strut array (count this+0x130, base this+0x134); recorded as a conflict, not a merge. MatrixVectorHelpers element widths (double vs float) conflict at shared offsets 0x00..0x20; recorded as a conflict. The two LDLT solver kernels share workspace region 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 but disjoint matrix buffers; relationship unresolved. Trust is DERIVED/GUESS throughout; all owners remain UNKNOWN at the function-IR level. State machines: none proposed.

engine_subsystems.name: CollisionGeometryAndSpatialQuery
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Collision-geometry container and nearest-neighbor spatial queries over strut arrays, node chains, and spatial trees. Functions from two proposals (CollisionModel and SpatialNearestNeighborQuery) operate on a shared 316-byte-stride strut array (count +0x130, base +0x134) and a 28-byte-stride struct array (+0x154); cross-family ownership of the container is unresolved.

engine_subsystems.name: MathAndVectorPrimitives
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Stateless geometric/vector math primitives: ray-sphere intersection, 2D direction projection, SSE two-point interpolation, 3x3 matrix-by-vector multiply, Euler-to-matrix conversion, per-frame matrix/vector frame-buffer setup, and embedded-array zero-init. Pure helpers; no proven shared class.

engine_subsystems.name: PackedVectorCodec
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Decode compact int16-packed vector records into float vectors with documented scale factors (1/2048, 0.02, 1/512); used on per-frame physics and audio parameter paths.

engine_subsystems.name: SparseConstraintSolver
engine_subsystems.responsibility: Standalone global-workspace block LDL^T factorization and substitution-solve kernels for sparse dynamics constraint matrices (0x0056FA96, 0x00575BBD); no parameters, no callees, return 0; operate on global double workspaces indexed by row-pointer tables.

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionPrimitives
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Stateless geometric/vector math primitives: ray-sphere quadratic intersection (suspension contact), 2D direction projection, SSE two-point linear interpolation. Grouped by shape only; owner identity not proven (GUESS).
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Two float32 samples at this+0x0/+0x8 (x/z of a 2D direction vector) are boundary clues for 0x00423AD0 only. The other two methods carry no instance fields; treat the family as stateless, not as a struct layout.

canonical_type_families.name: CollisionModel
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Collision-geometry container owning a 316-byte-stride element (strut) array at +0x134 (count +0x130), a 28-byte-stride struct array at +0x154, and further owned buffers +0x150/+0x158; supports nearest-neighbor query, indexed struct reads, and destructor-style teardown freeing every owned allocation. Name descriptive; owner identity UNKNOWN.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Count +0x130 and base +0x134 (316-byte stride) describe the strut array; +0x154 the 28-byte-stride struct array; +0x150/+0x158 additional owned buffers; +0x148 teardown sentinel (-1.0f); +0x138 reset state (role unknown). Field samples are boundary clues, not a complete layout; the 316-byte element struct is undefined.

canonical_type_families.name: SparseConstraintSolver
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Two standalone block LDL^T factorization/substitution-solve kernels over global double constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer tables; no instance state, no parameters, no callees, return 0. Grouped by shared algorithm and overlapping workspace region; two phases of one solver vs two kernels is not provable.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: No instance fields (field_count 0). All state lives in global double workspaces and row-pointer tables; the full global address set is carried in unresolved_evidence_refs as unresolved workspace layout (roles of the 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 diagonals not decidable).

canonical_type_families.name: SpatialNearestNeighborQuery
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Nearest-neighbor lookups over strut arrays, BVH chains, and spatial trees (AI steering / racing-line code). Shared node concepts (position, plane coefficients, links, identifier) appear across all three methods, but common ownership is unproven; 0x00403AA0 falls back to 0x004038E0.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Query-position floats +0/+4/+8 (from 0x004039C0) and strut array +0x130/+0x134 (from 0x004038E0) are boundary clues. Element/node layout (position +148/+152/+156, plane coefficients +164/+172, links +268/+272, identifier +300, path length +60) is documented in prose but carries no field evidence refs and is NOT placed as fields; fields +0x1C8..+0x260 read by 0x004038E0 are listed but absent from the raw source.

canonical_type_families.name: MatrixVectorHelpers
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Pure matrix/vector math: 3x3 matrix-by-vector multiply (doubles) and Euler-angle to rotation-matrix conversion (floats). Grouping is a DERIVED proposal; element widths differ so shared offsets may be distinct storage.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Shared offsets 0x00..0x20 are read as 8-byte doubles (8-byte stride) by 0x00435E00 and written as 4-byte floats (4-byte stride) by 0x00566E40; the width conflict means the samples must not be merged into one layout. Treat offsets as per-function boundary clues, not a proven common struct.

canonical_type_families.name: PackedShortVectorRecord
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Compressed int16 vector codecs: unpack compact records to floats with documented scale factors (1/2048, 0.02, 1/512). Three distinct record layouts under one base; common ownership of a single record struct is unproven.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Three disjoint layouts: (a) raw dwords +0x0/+0x4/+0x8 plus int16s +0xC/+0xE/+0x10 scaled 1/2048; (b) int16s +0x1E/+0x20/+0x22 scaled 0.02; (c) int16s +0x28/+0x2A scaled 1/512 with Y zeroed. Each sample is a boundary clue for its own function; do not assume one struct.

canonical_type_families.name: PhysicsFrameTransform
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Per-frame vehicle physics transform setup: store a 3x3 rotation matrix, input vector, and matrix-by-vector product in a frame buffer at base+0x34B0; returns a pointer to the stored matrix. Called per frame from VehiclePhysicsTimeStep.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: Frame-buffer samples at +0x34B0 (9 floats, rotation matrix), +0x3534 (3 floats, input vector), +0x3540 (3 floats, output product). Boundary clue for a larger vehicle-physics frame struct, not a standalone type.

canonical_type_families.name: EmbeddedArrayBlock
canonical_type_families.responsibility: Zero-initialize a 16-dword (0x40-byte) embedded array block (this+0x0..+0x3C) and return this; called from physics-defaults and tire-model-data initialization to clear embedded arrays.
canonical_type_families.field_policy: 16 dword samples at +0x0..+0x3C are the zeroed block; embedded inside larger construction objects, not a standalone type.

interfaces.name: ISpatialQuery
interfaces.purpose: Nearest-node / nearest-strut spatial lookup used by AI steering and racing-line code, with optional strut-type filtering and plane-side rejection.

interfaces.name: ICompressedVectorCodec
interfaces.purpose: Decode compact int16-packed position/direction records into float vectors on the per-frame physics and audio paths.

compatibility_contracts.name: SuspensionRaySphereContact
compatibility_contracts.description: Ray-sphere quadratic intersection used by the vehicle suspension force calculation: takes six doubles, returns 0.0 on any miss and 1/sqrt(p) as a penetration-length proxy on hit. Must remain a pure scalar float-returning function with no side effects or callees.

compatibility_contracts.name: CollisionModelOwnedBufferLayout
compatibility_contracts.description: The collision container owns pointer buffers at +0x150/+0x154/+0x158 and a 316-byte-stride element array at +0x134 (count +0x130) whose allocation is length-prefixed 4 bytes before the base. Teardown frees each non-null buffer via FreeWrapper_7bcf, runs per-element release (0x004B0170) over the element array, frees the array allocation, nulls the pointers, writes -1.0f at +0x148, clears +0x130/+0x134/+0x138, and returns the prior array base.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQueryResult
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor query walks linked collision nodes (next pointers at +0x110/+0x10C) and the strut array (316-byte stride, entries with type field at +0x12C <= 1 distance-tested), using a signed plane-distance probe (0x004FB6D0). Returns a node pointer, preferring the plane-verified candidate when its final signed distance is non-negative.

compatibility_contracts.name: SparseConstraintSolverWorkspace
compatibility_contracts.description: Two standalone LDLT solvers factor global double constraint-matrix workspaces (0x008CFBF0..0x008D3B60 and 0x008D2120..0x008D3978) indexed by global row-pointer arrays (0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 and 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0); both take no parameters and return 0. A replacement must keep these global buffers and pointer tables byte-compatible.

compatibility_contracts.name: NearestNeighborQuerySemantics
compatibility_contracts.description: Nearest-neighbor lookups must preserve the documented selection rules: zero-count early return (strut count at base+0x130 <= 0), strut-type filter (a3 == -1 or equals element type at +300), plane-side rejection selecting the linked +272 child, and the 200.0 accumulated path-length bound for chain traversal.

compatibility_contracts.name: ShortVectorPackingScale
compatibility_contracts.description: Compressed int16 vectors must decode with the packet's documented scale factors: 1/2048 for the 3-dword + 3-int16 record, 0.02 for the this[15..17] record, and 1/512 for the 2-component this[20]/this[21] record with the Y output component zeroed.

compatibility_contracts.name: MatrixVectorMultiplyReturnsInput
compatibility_contracts.description: The 3x3-by-vector multiply must return the input vector pointer; the Euler conversion must produce a row-major 3x3 rotation matrix with no side effects; MatrixVectorSetup must return a pointer to the stored matrix.

conflicts.subject: Ownership of the 316-byte-stride strut array (count this+0x130, base this+0x134)
alternatives: CollisionModel (proposal:class:math_and_collision_01:1) owns the container and queries it via 0x00403640
SpatialNearestNeighborQuery (proposal:class:wave_001_math_and_collision_01:0) queries the same layout via 0x004038E0/0x00403AA0, possibly as reader of a shared container
Two independent strut arrays with an identical layout
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. Both proposals describe nearest-neighbor queries over the same strut-array layout; the packet proves the layout, not the owner. Do not merge CollisionModel and SpatialNearestNeighborQuery into one class without explicit owner evidence.

conflicts.subject: Element width at shared offsets 0x00..0x20 in MatrixVectorHelpers
alternatives: double (8-byte) storage read by 0x00435E00 at 8-byte stride
float (4-byte) storage written by 0x00566E40 at 4-byte stride
one struct with padding or type reinterpretation
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. The packet cannot distinguish one double array from two float arrays at the same offsets; keep the two methods' layouts separate.

conflicts.subject: Relationship between the two LDLT solver kernels 0x0056FA96 and 0x00575BBD
alternatives: Two phases of one constraint solver
Two solver instances sharing a workspace region
conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. They share overlapping global workspace (0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 touched by both) but use disjoint matrix buffers; not provable from the packet.

unresolved: CollisionPrimitives grouping is by shape only (stateless math helpers): the packet assigns each function an UNKNOWN owner and proves no shared class; 0x00401180 is used by the suspension path, 0x00423AD0 by an AI/opponent proximity path, and 0x0051F6A0 has no callers.
CollisionModel name is descriptive; owner identity UNKNOWN. Field +0x138 is only observed being reset to 0 in teardown; its live role is unknown.

CollisionModel node-link offsets +0x110/+0x10C and strut-entry type selector +0x12C are documented in prose (see 0x00403640) but have no allowed field evidence refs, so no field entry can model them without inventing a ref.

0x00401180: roles of the six double inputs (a1..a6) are inferred from call context only; three read-only double globals (dbl_59E420, dbl_59E428, dbl_59E430) flagged by packet facts do not appear in the raw source.

0x00403640: meaning of read-only globals flt_59E440, flt_59E468, flt_59E46C not visible in raw source; the 4x-weighted Z component in the squared-distance score is unexplained; semantics of node link offsets +0x110/+0x10C unknown; type selector at entry+0x12C enum values beyond <= 1 unknown.

0x00403F70: element size is 28 bytes but only 24 bytes are copied (remaining 4 unread); array base this+0x154 is read-only here and the meaning of the two output blocks is not established; the DERIVED prelabel 'getter' is too weak (raw source outranks it).
0x004045F0: EmptyStub_0170 (0x004B0170) per-element behavior (release vs no-op) is outside the packet; the 316-byte element struct is undefined.

0x0051F6A0: a5/a6 passed as unsigned ints and reinterpreted as floats via shuffle (type not determinable); only high halves of each double are used; no caller/callee evidence for what the two-point vectors encode.

0x0056FA96: exact role of workspace diagonals 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 (RHS vector, D-factor, or solve accumulator) not decidable; whether the final tail is strictly backward substitution or an interleaved block-triangular solve is ambiguous; pointer tables 0x008D3988..0x008D3A24 point at runtime row bases not present in the packet; return-0 contract unconfirmed (no static callers).

0x00575BBD: pointer array 0x008D3B68..0x008D3BF0 holds runtime row bases outside this function; numeric immediates are absolute addresses encoded as 32-bit constants (equivalence to named globals is by address match only); block sizes DERIVED from loop bounds, not confirmed; LDLT vs Cholesky interpretation DERIVED from the reciprocal-diagonal + rank-1-update pattern; exact forward/backward solve split not confirmed.

The two solver functions share overlapping global workspace region 0x008D3A28..0x008D3B60 but operate on disjoint matrix buffers; whether they are two phases of one solver, two solver instances, or two independent kernels is not provable from the packet.

Strut/node element layouts (position +148/+152/+156, plane coefficients +164/+172, type +300, linked child +272, sibling link +268, child-select +276, path length +60, stride 316) are DERIVED from the decompilation; the packet carries no field table for these element types and they are not placed as class fields.
Fields this+0x1C8, +0x1CC, +0x1D0, +0x1D8, +0x1E0, +0x244, +0x260 are listed as read by 0x004038E0 but do not appear in the raw source text; their role is unknown.
Globals flt_59E440, flt_59E4D8, flt_59E6EC, flt_59E77C are read per packet facts but their read sites and meaning are not visible in the raw source (scale literals are inlined).
Whether node+272 is a child pointer or a sibling link is inferred from existing analysis; not provable from this packet alone.
The meaning of the 200.0 bound (flt_59E470) as a search radius is DERIVED; the raw source only compares the accumulated path length against it.

0x00435E00 reads 8-byte doubles at 8-byte stride while 0x00566E40 writes 4-byte floats at 4-byte stride; shared offsets 0x00..0x20 may belong to distinct storage, so the MatrixVectorHelpers grouping is DERIVED and unproven (see conflict MatrixVectorHelpersElementWidth).
PackedShortVectorRecord groups three distinct record layouts (0x0..0x10, 0x1E..0x22, 0x28..0x2A) under one base; common ownership of a single record struct is unproven.

SpatialNearestNeighborQuery groups three functions whose common ownership is unproven: query-position fields (+0/4/8) come from 0x004039C0 only, strut fields (+0x130/+0x134) from 0x004038E0 only, and 0x00403AA0's own use of this-fields is not evidenced by packet operations.
The role of the output vector written by 0x004F17D0 within the per-frame physics step is not described in the packet.

Callers (AISteering 0x004270A0, VehiclePhysicsTimeStep 0x004C73F0, AudioParameterInterpolation 0x004FF680, PhysicsDefaultsInitializer 0x004F2B50, TireModelDataInit 0x004F34E0) are known only through evidence refs; no caller-side packet data is available.
Input angles a1[0..2] of 0x00566E40 are read via pointer arithmetic, not through the this-based field evidence list.
